title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame

summary.text: The Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame investigation aims to characterize weak coflow methane and ethylene diffusion flames and their sooting tendencies to provide data for testing computational models.

flow.text: Coflow velocity and fuel dilution are listed as varied parameters; no values are given.

measurements.text: Thin-filament pyrometry, OH* and CH* chemiluminescence, soot luminosity and laser extinction.

claims.text: The investigation aims to characterize the behavior of weak coflow diffusion flames of methane and ethylene as a function of velocity and fuel dilution, to provide experimental data for rigorous testing of computational models.
The investigation aims to characterize the sooting tendencies of diffusion flames with long residence times, as a function of velocity and fuel dilution.
The source states that the investigation was focused on gathering bench mark data to validate computation models, rather than stating a testable hypothesis of its own.
The source states that understanding the factors that affect flame extinction in diffusion flames is critical in the suppression of fires.

limitations.text: The hypothesis field refers to publications for details and does not itself state a hypothesis.
This draft cites PSI metadata and no PDF text. The packet also includes official table passages whose findings have not been incorporated or reviewed.

modeling_resources.description: Experimental table for the CLD Flame investigation, relevant to flame temperature, chemiluminescence and soot measurements.

Flame temperatures in non-sooting regions will be measured using thin-filament pyrometry.
The sooting tendencies of the more fuel-rich flames will be investigated using soot luminosity and laser extinction measurements to determine soot temperatures and soot volume fractions.
measurements will be made of flame chemiluminesence of OH* and CH* to observe variations in lift-off height and flame shape as extinction limits are approached.
an understanding of those factors that affect flame extinction in diffusion flames is critical in the suppression of fires

The enhanced time and spatial scales in a microgravity environment will be important for achieving both goals.
